title: Capture a host's real hook payload through hooks/run.cjs, not docs or settings
body:
In a checkout session, temporarily make hooks/run.cjs append stdin (or filtered env) for the event to a scratch file, trigger the tool call, read it, then git checkout hooks/run.cjs. Do not trust documentation summaries for the shape, and do not plan on registering new events in .claude/settings.local.json from the agent: auto mode refuses that edit as self-modification, so an event not yet registered needs the user or a plugin-dir session.

Why: On 2026-09-24 this captured Claude Code's real PostToolUse Bash shape ({stdout, stderr, interrupted, ...}, no exit code) and CLAUDECODE=1 in hook env, while a docs-derived summary claimed tool_response was {type, text}. Adding PostToolUseFailure to settings.local.json was denied by the permission classifier.

evidence.summary: Validation recorded after the observe fix, from a real Claude Code PostToolUse without exit code.
Launcher every checkout hook runs through; edits take effect on the next hook call.
Comment records the shapes captured this way.
Anchored delivery: keywords validated against this memory's own text and a generic-request corpus before proposing.

v1.trigger: when a hook change depends on the exact payload a host sends (tool_response fields, event names, environment)
